verifications.claim: Artemis II successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' 'The Artemis II mission is launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'launched on 1 April 2026 at 6.35pm Eastern Time'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on date, time, location, and successful launch across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II lifted off on a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R5: 'Launching aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R5: 'four astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as four astronauts across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day mission to orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'not ... go into lunar orbit. Instead ... loop around it' 'nine and a half days'; R3: 'approximately 10-day ... around the Moon'; R5: 'orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission ... looped around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Duration ~10 days supported; 'orbit' contradicted by R1 (explicitly not lunar orbit) vs. R5 (says orbit).

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R6: 'first people to enter lunar space since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R7: 'first time in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches timeline since Apollo (1972-2026 >50 years).

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch' 'only the second SLS launch, and the first one carrying astronauts'; R3: 'first crewed mission of the Artemis program'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first crewed SLS after uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule ... making only its second flight — and its first with a crew on board'; R3: 'first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as first crewed after uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is designed to test systems and orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule' 'not ... lunar orbit ... loop around it'; R3: 'test the systems and hardware'; R5: 'orbit the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Test systems clearly supported; 'orbit the Moon' contradicted (R1 explicit no lunar orbit vs. R5 says orbit).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and affiliations match across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch had minor, expected technical issues.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'higher-than-expected temperature reading from a sensor ... instrumentation issue'; 'temporary loss of communication ... resolved ... not considered a major issue'; R3: 'engineers investigated a sensor ... believed to be an instrumentation issue'
verifications.reasoning: Minor issues (sensor, comm) supported and resolved; 'expected' broader/inferred from routine troubleshooting, not explicit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch had a temporary sensor issue.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'higher-than-expected temperature reading from a sensor on the launch abort system's ... battery'; R3: 'sensor on the launch abort system’s attitude control motor controller battery ... higher temperature than would be expected'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches temporary sensor issue during launch countdown.

verifications.claim: The temporary sensor issue did not affect the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'believed to be an instrumentation issue and will not affect today's launch'; R3: 'believed to be an instrumentation issue and will not affect today’s launch'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as not affecting launch/mission.

verifications.claim: After launching, the Orion spacecraft is scheduled to separate from the upper stage of the rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule separated from the interim cryogenic propulsion stage'; R3: 'core stage separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage'
verifications.reasoning: Directly describes post-launch separation from upper stage (ICPS).

verifications.claim: After launching, the Orion spacecraft is scheduled to proceed with its lunar journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'before finally heading for the moon'; R3: 'outbound journey to the Moon'; R4: 'on their way to journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm progression to lunar trajectory after launch and tests.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is part of NASA's program to return humans to the Moon and pave the way for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis program'; R3: 'pave the way for future lunar landings'; R5: 'pave the way for long-term exploration ... on the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as part of Artemis program for Moon return and future landings.
